statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 62% (elevated), Confidence 75% (high).
recommendation: Tail sits at its floor because CME equity-index futures remain halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path exists to trend. Stress stays elevated on the unresolved US-Iran tanker exchange with Brent at a six-week high. One narrow window is flagged: the 22:00Z Globex restart, mapped to WATCH for a single hour.
headline: Second hour of the Labor Day futures halt; risk stays concentrated at the 22:00Z restart
body: CME equity-index futures have now been halted for more than ninety minutes, having closed at 17:00Z, while NYSE and Nasdaq stayed shut all day for Labor Day and reopen Tuesday at 13:30Z. The last NQ print remains 29,565.25, up 40.50 points (+0.14%), inside a narrow 29,530.50-29,682.50 holiday range that had faded from its high, so the pre-halt tape showed working retracements and no one-way structure. With no order book at all, there is no price path that can deny mean reversion, which is why Tail sits at its floor; the same absence removes the evidence a forward read would normally rest on. The live risk stays in energy and shipping. Brent is $97.34, up about 1.1% and at a six-week high after touching roughly $97.9 intraday, with WTI near $92.74, following US strikes on three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday and Iranian claims of retaliation against six vessels. US Central Command reports redirecting 92 commercial vessels, disabling three and boarding two, and Kpler-tracked Hormuz transits are running near 13 vessels a day against about 20 million barrels flowing before the conflict. Set against that, equities have so far absorbed the shock: Monday's Asian cash session closed firmly higher, with the Nikkei up 2.12% and the Kospi up 4.61%, while Europe finished mixed with the Stoxx 600 just below flat. VIX last printed 15.30 at Friday's close and the 3 September H.15 data last showed 4.34% at two years and 4.77% at ten years; neither refreshes on the holiday. That combination is cross-asset conflict, which widens uncertainty without producing the persistent no-retracement path that defines Tail, so Stress stays elevated while Tail does not. No new verified escalation has landed since the halt began. The structural risk remains mechanical: several hours of unpriced headlines clearing into a thin 22:00Z restart, which is why the danger window is a single hour rather than session-wide. A secondary checkpoint is Tuesday's 13:30Z cash reopen, the first regular session after a three-day weekend. The week's principal macro risk sits Thursday with PPI and jobless claims and Friday with August CPI. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was available but timestamped 13:03Z, well beyond the ninety-minute freshness limit, so it was not used as supporting evidence.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the last twenty-four hourly Claude assessments are available; the 2026-09-06T21:00Z slot has no published assessment and is marked unavailable. The window was uniformly green with EA_ON throughout and Tail between 5% and 10%. Stress rose from a 54-58% band overnight to 61-64% through the US afternoon as crude extended and holiday liquidity thinned, then held at 63% into the halt. Confidence eased from 86% to 76% over the same stretch as live price evidence disappeared. Dominant mode was normal except the 14:00Z, 16:00Z and 17:00Z slots, which were mixed as the energy-versus-equity divergence widened.
outlookSummary: The next twenty-four hours are shaped by market structure rather than macro. Futures stay halted until 22:00Z, so the first four forecast hours carry no tradable price path and Tail sits at its floor. The single elevated slot is the 22:00Z restart, where several hours of unpriced US-Iran escalation would meet the thinnest liquidity of the window; Tail is mapped to WATCH there for one hour only. Path risk then decays through the Asian and European sessions as depth rebuilds, with a secondary rise into the 13:30Z US cash reopen, the first regular session after the three-day weekend. All post-halt structure is framed conditionally because none of it is observable at the assessment cutoff; only the pre-halt range and fade are stated as fact. NFIB at 10:00Z and the weekly ADP print at 12:15Z are the scheduled US releases inside the window, while the week's principal checkpoints - PPI and jobless claims Thursday, August CPI Friday - fall outside it.
